en: Now,
another neat feature
is that you can select code,
open this edit mode, but you can now not
just pass edit instructions to Cursor, but
instead you can also write a quick question
like,
what does this code do?
What does
extended false mean? Why is it not true?
You can also bring in the web, let's say, so
that Cursor does a web search if it needs
to.
And now instead of clicking Generate, which
would try to generate some code, which
doesn't make a lot of sense for this prompt,
you can pick Quick Question or use this
shortcut here.
And now you really just have a normal chat
here where the goal now is not to generate
code, but instead to generate an answer for
your question
so that you'll learn what this code does and
what extended false is and why it's set like
this.
You can also click on the source here to
learn more.
So that's a nice, quick and easy way to
learn more about parts of your code or to
quickly understand more about certain parts
of your code, which of course is especially
helpful if you're maybe working in a team
and you
didn't write some code on your own.
Or it's simply been some time since you last
wrote some code here, well, then you can use
this quick question mode.
